dedupe_keys.name: italian hospital beds discharges and inpatient days by hospital and discipline 2010 and 2017 bed management indicators

description: This workbook compiles how many beds each Italian hospital had, and how intensively they were used, in 2010 and 2017, to show how much slack intensive care and other wards had before the COVID-19 outbreak. The producers are Fabrizio Pecoraro, Fabrizio Clemente and Daniela Luzi of Italy's National Research Council, who collected the figures from the Ministry of Health's open data and published them with a paper on intensive care bed management in April 2020. Coverage is Italy by hospital structure and discipline for the two years. Sheets give beds, discharges and inpatient days, plus bed management indicators the authors computed to assess the efficiency of ordinary bed use. The file is available as a free XLSX download from Zenodo under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 licence, and newer years can be taken from the ministry's portal. Caveats: only two years, hospital codes need matching to locations from other sources, and indicators assume the ministry's bed counts reflect staffed beds. Simulation uses: estimating surge capacity by hospital and region for epidemics or mass casualty events, and calibrating bed occupancy in hospital system models. Related records: the Italian accessibility data (data-italy-hospital-accessibility-gravity-hip-replacement) come from the same author, and the WHO health infrastructure indicators (data-who-gho-health-infrastructure-indicators) give national bed counts.
